# userParametersTest.py

You can view and download this file on Github: [userParametersTest.py](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/tree/master/python/TestModels/userParametersTest.py)

```{code-block} python
:linenos:

#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
# This is an EXUDYN example
#
# Details:  The parameters of a user item (#3056): two mass-spring oscillators as ObjectUserBody on NodePoint, each
#           with its own mass and stiffness in its parameter vector, named by a ParameterLayout. The user functions
#           get the reference coordinates qRef, the displacements q, the velocities q_t and the parameters; the
#           spring acts on q. One recorded symbolic force and mass matrix serve both bodies, and a parameter changed
#           with SetObjectParameter acts without recording again. The solutions agree with the Python user functions
#           and with x0 cos(sqrt(k/m) t). With constantMassMatrix, the mass matrix user function is called once per
#           body and the solution is the same (#3058).
#
# Author:   Johannes Gerstmayr
# Date:     2026-10-22
#
# Copyright:This file is part of Exudyn. Exudyn is free software. You can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the Exudyn license. See 'LICENSE.txt' for more details.
#
#+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

import exudyn as exu
from exudyn.utilities import * #includes itemInterface and rigidBodyUtilities
from exudyn.advancedUtilities import CreateSymbolicUserFunction, ParameterLayout
import exudyn.cMath as cMath
import numpy as np
esym = exu.symbolic

#the layout of the parameters of this kind of user body
layout = ParameterLayout([('mass', 1), ('stiffness', 1)])

massCalls = [0] #the calls of UFmass
def UFmass(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    massCalls[0] += 1
    return layout.ToDict(parameters)['mass']*np.eye(3)

def UFforce(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    return -layout.ToDict(parameters)['stiffness']*q

def UFmassSymbolic(mbs, t, itemNumber, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    return layout.ToDict(parameters)['mass']*esym.Matrix(np.eye(3))

def UFposition(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    return qRef + q + localPosition

def UFpositionJacobian(mbs, t, itemNumber, localPosition, qRef, q, q_t, parameters):
    return np.eye(3)

values = [{'mass': 2., 'stiffness': 50.}, {'mass': 0.5, 'stiffness': 200.}]
x0 = 0.1        #initial displacement
endTime = 0.5

simulationSettings = exu.SimulationSettings()
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.numberOfSteps = 5000
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.endTime = endTime
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.verboseMode = 0
simulationSettings.solution.file.write = False

def Solve(kind, changedStiffness=None, constantMassMatrix=False):
    """the two oscillators with Python ('python') or one recording of symbolic ('symbolic') user functions; the
    displacement of each at endTime"""
    SC = exu.SystemContainer()
    mbs = SC.AddSystem()
    bodies = []
    for (i, value) in enumerate(values):
        node = mbs.AddNode(NodePoint(referenceCoordinates=[1. + i, 0, 0], initialCoordinates=[x0, 0, 0]))
        bodies.append(mbs.AddObject(ObjectUserBody(nodeNumbers=[node], parameters=layout.ToVector(value), constantMassMatrix=constantMassMatrix,
                                                   massMatrixUserFunction=UFmass, forceUserFunction=UFforce,
                                                   positionUserFunction=UFposition,
                                                   positionJacobianUserFunction=UFpositionJacobian)))
    if kind == 'symbolic': #recorded once, for the first body, and given to both
        keep = [CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs, UFforce, 'forceUserFunction', bodies[0]),
                CreateSymbolicUserFunction(mbs, UFmassSymbolic, 'massMatrixUserFunction', bodies[0])]
        for body in bodies:
            mbs.SetObjectParameter(body, 'forceUserFunction', keep[0])
            mbs.SetObjectParameter(body, 'massMatrixUserFunction', keep[1])
        mbs.variables['keep'] = keep
    if changedStiffness is not None: #after the recording: no new recording needed
        mbs.SetObjectParameter(bodies[1], 'parameters', layout.ToVector({'mass': values[1]['mass'], 'stiffness': changedStiffness}))
    mbs.Assemble()
    mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings)
    return [mbs.GetObjectOutputBody(body, exu.OutputVariableType.Displacement, localPosition=[0, 0, 0])[0] for body in bodies]

python = Solve('python')
symbolic = Solve('symbolic')
exact = [x0*cMath.cos(cMath.sqrt(value['stiffness']/value['mass'])*endTime) for value in values]
exu.Print('displacements, Python:', python, ', symbolic:', symbolic, ', exact:', exact)

massCalls[0] = 0
constant = Solve('python', constantMassMatrix=True)
exu.Print('constant mass matrix: calls of the mass matrix function', massCalls[0], ', displacements', constant)

changed = Solve('symbolic', changedStiffness=50.)
exactChanged = x0*cMath.cos(cMath.sqrt(50./values[1]['mass'])*endTime)
exu.Print('the stiffness of body 1 changed after the recording:', changed[1], ', exact:', exactChanged)

u = 0
u += int(max(abs(python[i] - symbolic[i]) for i in range(2)) > 1e-12)       #one recording, two parameter sets
u += int(max(abs(python[i] - exact[i]) for i in range(2)) > 1e-5)           #the time integration
u += int(abs(changed[1] - exactChanged) > 1e-5) + int(abs(changed[0] - symbolic[0]) > 1e-14)
u += int(layout.Size() != 2) + int(list(layout.ToVector({'stiffness': 3., 'mass': 4.})) != [4., 3.])
refused = 0
for wrong in [{'mass': 1.}, {'mass': 1., 'stiffness': 1., 'damping': 1.}, {'mass': [1., 2.], 'stiffness': 1.}]:
    try:
        layout.ToVector(wrong)
    except ValueError:
        refused += 1
u += 3 - refused
u += int(massCalls[0] != 2) + int(max(abs(python[i] - constant[i]) for i in range(2)) > 1e-14)   #once per body, the same solution

exu.Print('solution of userParametersTest=', u + symbolic[0] + symbolic[1])

exu.sys['testResult'] = u + symbolic[0] + symbolic[1]
```
